newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hoechst gave Paris assurances on Roussel.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst gave Paris assurances on Roussel.

text.p: German chemicals giant Hoechst AG gave undertakings to the French government as part of negotiations over its buy-out of Roussel-Uclaf, Hoechst's finance director said on Wednesday.

"One of (Roussel's) major shareholders is the ERAP state-owned holding company," Klaus Schmieder told a news conference. "We decided to go into discussions and ended up discussing with the French government, in a friendly manner, the commitments we would undertake."

After the buy-out, Roussel will maintain pre-clinical and clinical development in France, as well as run a major research centre at Romainville on the Paris suburbs, continue chemicals manufacture and create 700 new jobs for young people from January 1, of this year to 1999.
It will also maintain 220 million franc financing for various research programmes with public health authorities.
Roussel had 1995 group net profit, excluding exceptionals, of 1.33 billion francs, on sales of 16.47 billion. It spent 1.92 billion in research and development and employed 14,300.

The issue of commitments to maintaining jobs and investment by foreign companies taking over French companies has come under the spotlight recently following a rejection by the Privatisation Commission of a bid by South Korea's Daewoo Electronics for Thomson Multimedia (TMM).
The commission said Daewoo's offer failed to give satisfactory commitments on maintaining jobs in the French company, which makes consumer electronics.
